items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I marvel at the fact that Paul Jeffrey (PHONETIC) give me a record date back there in '72... and Paul did all the arrangements on that.

ctx.x: But then, too, there's a problem that Chris talks about is there's no guarantee of where they'll go back to. It's like Stanley Clarke (PHONETIC) never having heard of John Kirby. Because the collective improvisation, that approach to playing the fiddle is not taught. There's no guarantee what people will learn or where they'll go.

Well, that's true, but most of them think, "Oh, I know music backwards and forward," you know, that they qualify to play anything. But that's not the way it is really. To play just straight-ahead music. Anybody can write anything for you. They write solos for guys and they can play them. I marvel at the fact that Paul Jeffrey (PHONETIC) give me a record date back there in '72, you know, after you and I met, and Paul did all the arrangements on that. I'm looking at the music; he knew (unintelligible) to write…
